newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi.
biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
GUJARAT GOVERNMENT FEARS PRESIDENT'S RULE

The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Gujarat charged the Governor with plans to pull down the government and demanded his recall. There were reports the Governor had recommended the imposition of President's rule in Gujarat. The Governor's office denied the reports. It said the Governor had only apprised the President about the current political situation in the state. The deputy Speaker has so far suspended the Assembly twice, denying the BJP a chance to prove its strength in the Assembly. The BJP needed to meet this requirement after a split in the party. The Assembly is next meeting on September 18.
The Pioneer
TELECOMMUNICATION SCAM A PLOT TO DISCREDIT CONGRESS CHIEF

Former communications minister Sukh Ram said the telecom scam was part of a plot to discredit former prime minister Narasimha Rao. Sukh Ram was referring to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into graft charges against him. "I am a pawn in political intrigues for power," he said. Sukh Ram was summoned by CBI following raids on his residences in India which led to recovery of $4 million worth of cash and assets. CBI is planning to question him in connection with telecom equipment supply scandal and violation of Income Tax Act.
The Times Of India
SCAM-TAINTED EX-MINISTER RETURNING TODAY

Former communications minister Sukh Ram may return home on Monday. Sukh Ram, currently stationed in Britain, is facing corruption charges following the recovery of 36.6 million rupees in cash by the investigating agencies from his houses. Reports said the former minister was planning to further extend his stay in London on grounds of ill health. However, his son in law informed that Sukh Ram had no plans to stay back in Britain any longer and was returning home on Monday.
Business Standard
GOVERNMENT ABANDONS GOLDEN SHARE OPTION IN STATE FIRMS

The Government has dropped plans to issue golden shares for retaining control over public sector units after privatisation. The move follows the Government's decision not to go in for 100 percent divestment in any area, including in the non core sector. The internal ceiling for divestment in all sectors has now been set at 74 percent. The concept of golden shares has become irrelevant as the Government has decided to retain 26 percent stake in all sectors. The golden shares carry veto powers which enable the holder to block management resolutions which go against his interests.
UNIT TRUST TO SET UP $100 MLN DEBT FUND ABROAD

The Unit Trust of India (UTI) may set up a dedicated debt fund overseas with an initial corpus of $100 million. UTI plans to expand the corpus depending on market response. This would be the first dedicated debt fund to be floated overseas by any Indian organisation. UTI's move follows the Finance Ministry's decision to permit Foreign Institutional Investors to put in their entire corpus in corporate debt as against the earlier limit of 30 percent. UTI is setting up offices in Dubai and London.
NAPHTHA USE IN POWER PLANTS MAY BE BANNED

The new liquid fuel policy being prepared by the Power Ministry may not allow use of naphtha as primary fuel for power generation. The use of high speed diesel is already prohibited. The Power Ministry's decision was influenced by the Petroleum Ministry's view that naptha would cease to be a surplus fuel in the country in the very near future. According to the Petroleum Ministry, naptha availability will shrink in the coming years all over the world making its use in power plants unviable.
The Economic Times
HCL CORP TO BUY HEWLETT PACKARD SHARE IN JOINT VENTURE

Computer major HCL Corp is negotiating with Hewlett Packard (HP) to acquire its equity stake in their seven billion rupee joint venture (JV) HCL-Hewlett Packard. HP plans to sell its stake in the JV because the revenues cannot be consolidated in the parent's balance sheet. Hewlett Packard may set up another JV with HCL for personal computers where it will hold a majority stake of 51 percent, say sources.
WORLD BANK WARNS AGAINST SLUGGISH POWER REFORMS

The World Bank (WB) has asked India to step up power sector reforms. WB has conveyed its unhappiness over the slow pace of reforms in the power sector to the Power Ministry. The Bank was aware of the problems the country faced in reforming its energy sector. However, the World Bank felt its recommendations for the power sector were not being properly implemented. It is feared that the Bank may stop giving aid to the Indian power sector after December 1996, as it may be hard to fulfil the conditions set by the lending institution.
Financial Express
MMTC LTD'S JEWELLERY TO GLITTER IN GLOBAL MARKETS

Super star trading house, MMTC Ltd, plans to enter the global market for direct export of gold jewellery. It plans to open a retail outlet at its New York office and tie up with reputed jwellary makers at home. MMTC's retail outfit at New York may become operational this year end. MMTC also plans to open duty free shops in the South Asia region, where there is a heavy inflow of foreign tourists. MMTC plans to open its first duty free shop in the Maldives.
NATIONAL BOURSE TURNOVER SOARS

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) fell to the third place in terms of turnover in fiscal 1995/96 (April-March). Reasons: the newly set up National Stock Exchange (NSE) has acquired most of its business. The total turnover of all the bourses rose by 45.72 percent during fiscal 1995/96. Whereas, BSE's turnover fell from 677.48 billion rupees in 1994/95 to 500 billion rupees in 1995/96, NSE increased its share in the total turnover from 1.06 percent in 1994-95 to 28.71 percent during last year to emerge as the premier bourse in country, said the 1995/96 annual report of the bourse regulator.
The Observer
BOMBAY BOURSE TO INTRODUCE INTERNATIONAL INDEX

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) is planning to introduce one more index in addition to the existing four. BSE president M.G. Damani said the new index would be of international standards and would be in place before the end of the year. The new international index would be formulated in accordance with the standards existing in developed markets, he added. Though the number of companies to be included in the new index is yet to be declared, all scrips which have entered the global depository receipt market are likely to find a place in the new index.
Business Line
MODILUFT PLANS $100 MLN CONSORTIUM LOAN

Modiluft has finalised a second line of credit for drawing $100 millions from a European consortium to fund its expansion plans. This is expected to fly the airline out of its present financial crisis and present it with a fresh route to fund its expansion plans. The airline is planning to seek permission for the external commercial borrowings from the Finance Ministry soon.
